# Sim Score

Background music written as code: ninety-two pieces in about fifty genres, in the spirit of SimCity, Spore,
The Sims and Second Life. Every note is composed in the browser a few bars before it plays (Tone.js, no
samples), so each performance is different and none of them ends.

**The houseband.** Pick a situation (hanging out, party, fight, chase, campfire, sleep, presentation, work,
explore, shopping, romance, mystery, training, celebrate) and an energy level, and the band chooses a fitting
tune and segues into it; drift the energy away from the tune and the drums, then the bass, lay out. Every piece
declares its own `situations` and `energy`; `site/catalog.js` holds the families and the tags of the first 24.

## Run

```bash
python3 tools/serve.py 4802     # then open http://localhost:4802
```

`site/dev.html` loads everything plus `Sim.measure(id)` for offline loudness checks.

## Saved recordings

Each piece is rendered offline (seed 1, three minutes, 44.1 kHz, through the master bus) to `renders/<id>.mp3`,
with `renders/index.json` listing title, genre, tempo, situations and energy. With the dev server running:

```bash
tools/render.sh 4 180     # 4 headless Chrome workers, 180 s each; skips pieces already rendered
```

A different take of any piece is one seed away: `Sim.exportPiece(id, { seed: 7 })` in `dev.html`.

## Layout

- `site/engine/theory.js`: pitch, chord-symbol parser, chord scales, voice-leading voicings, seeded rng
- `site/engine/compose.js`: melodic line generator (chord-tone anchors, scale/chromatic fills, motifs)
- `site/engine/instruments.js`: the synth orchestra, level-calibrated so `volume: 0` means the same loudness everywhere
- `site/engine/more-instruments.js`: round three: drum machines (808, 909, Linn, Simmons), Latin, Brazilian, Japanese,
  Middle Eastern and West African percussion, slap and acid bass, supersaw, guitars, sax, koto, pedal steel, sidechain pump, tape, vinyl
- `site/engine/band.js`: the houseband (situation + energy → pick, segue, lay out)
- `site/catalog.js`: situations vocabulary, families, tags for the first 24 pieces
- `site/engine/conductor.js`: `Sim.register` contract; composes one cycle ahead, swing, humanize, layer muting, offline render
- `site/pieces/*.js`: one file per piece
- `tools/lint.mjs`, `tools/score.mjs`: check and print pieces in Node without audio (see `COMPOSING.md`)

## Adding a piece

Read `COMPOSING.md` (including the round-three brief), write `site/pieces/<id>.js` with `situations` and `energy`,
add its id to a family in `site/catalog.js`, then run `node tools/lint.mjs <id>` and read `node tools/score.mjs <id>`.
